question: ttft
answer:
TTFT and generation-rate tracking live in `ChatResult` (`src/nvidia_ai/llm.py:52`), populated inside `stream_chat()` (`src/nvidia_ai/llm.py:104`) as it reads the SSE stream — it timestamps the first content/reasoning delta into `ttft_s`/`ttft_content_s`/`ttft_reasoning_s`, the last delta into `last_token_s`, and stream close into `total_s`.

Two derived properties compute the rates:
- `ChatResult.decode_tps` (`src/nvidia_ai/llm.py:74`): `completion_tokens / (last_token_s - ttft_s)` — generation speed excluding TTFT, only returned when `completion_tokens >= MIN_TOKENS_FOR_TPS` and `gen_time >= MIN_GEN_TIME_S` to avoid noise on short answers.
- `ChatResult.e2e_tps` (`src/nvidia_ai/llm.py:90`): `completion_tokens / total_s` — end-to-end rate including TTFT.

The benchmark driver reads both into its per-attempt record via `_record()` (`src/nvidia_ai/bench.py:205`, referencing them at lines 223–224), which is called from `run()` (`src/nvidia_ai/bench.py:141`) after each `stream_chat()` call. `summarize()`/`to_markdown()` (`src/nvidia_ai/bench.py:238`, `283`) then aggregate TTFT, decode_tps, and e2e_tps (via `_median()`) into the report. `tests/test_llm.py:130` (`test_decode_tps_ignored_for_short_answers`) covers the short-answer guard.
